taskVersion.name: ves-heldout-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station H-08, survey area H. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 218.1 | 18.02 | 18.02
2 | 105.0 | 1.05 | 19.07
3 | 60.0 | 1.04 | 20.11
4 | 317.3 | 0.57 | 20.68
5 | 1743.2 | 5.17 | 25.85
6 | 2231.3 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as QHAA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station H-08, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station H-08, Survey Area H**

The interpreted VES model at H-08 comprises six layers. Resistivity decreases sharply from 218.1 Ω·m (Layer 1) to 105.0 Ω·m (Layer 2) and further to 60.0 Ω·m (Layer 3), indicating a conductive zone near 19–20 m depth. Below this, resistivity rises markedly through Layer 4 (317.3 Ω·m), Layer 5 (1743.2 Ω·m), and the basal Layer 6 (2231.3 Ω·m), suggesting a transition into a resistive substrate, possibly competent bedrock, beneath ~20 m.

Applying the standard curve-type notation to the resistivity sequence (218.1 > 105.0 > 60.0 < 317.3 < 1743.2 < 2231.3) gives triplet codes Q, H, A, A — consistent with the QHAA classification on file. The filed label accurately reflects the layer resistivity pattern.

{"curve_type_stated": "QHAA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
